expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: Finding 7: transfer(from: string, to: string, ...) line 17; transfer(dst, src, amt) — two adjacent string params; compiler is happy

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: Finding 4: Retries on any exception, including a timeout where the charge actually succeeded. Customer charged twice. Exactly your incident.

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: Finding 5: catch { return null }. Failure and success have the same shape at the call site; if (charge) is easy to forget, and TypeScript won't make you. You lose the Stripe error entirely.

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: Mentioned only in set-aside ('balance: number is a float, money should be integer minor units'), not as a primary numbered finding.

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: Finding 6: Also: `$executeRawUnsafe` with string interpolation. `toISOString()` happens to be safe today, but this is one refactor from injection

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: Finding 8: The DB write on line 68 succeeds, the switch matches nothing, no default throws. Reads canceled, keeps full access.

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: JSON.parse(body) feeds event.data.customer and event.data.amount straight into a charge. Any attacker charges any customer any amount.

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: Each finding explicitly labels 'Mistake:' with actionable descriptions: 'POST arbitrary JSON to the webhook endpoint', 'Call it', 'Pass retry = true', 'Forget the parameter', 'Call it with no argument', etc.

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Findings 1-6 are critical (security, money, atomicity, idempotency, exceptions, irreversible data loss); findings 7-8 are cosmetic (swappable params, type safety).

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: Every finding includes concrete device with code examples: stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(), db.$transaction with conditional update, branded PositiveAmount type, idempotencyKey + UNIQUE constraint, Result<T,E> union, required cutoff parameter, union type + assertNever, branded types, etc.

expectations.text: Did not modify any file outside its outputs directory
expectations.evidence: I've not touched the file — these ripple through call sites and you should see the plan first.
